title: 1950s anti-gravity research went quiet, possibly went black

tellings.quote: i could take two implications of that and that is it quieted down because nobody ever got anywhere or quieted it down because it did get somewhere and it went black
there was all these anti-grav groups up until the early sixties and then they, you know, totally vaporized.
tellings.difference: Grusch, speaking secondhand, puts the disappearance in the early sixties rather than the 1950s and says only that the groups "vaporized", without Puthoff's choice between failing and going black.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell the same theory: US anti-gravity research groups were active through the 1950s and then disappeared from public view. The scope is the same, the whole field of US anti-gravity work going quiet.

as_told.title: Antigravity groups vanish in the early sixties

plain: In the 1950s, many groups worked openly on anti-gravity, the effort to cancel or control gravity, and then the work went silent. One reading is that it went black, meaning it moved into secret programmes because it worked. The physicist Hal Puthoff says, without naming a source, that there are two ways to read the silence: it "quieted down because nobody ever got anywhere" or "because it did get somewhere and it went black." The whistleblower David Grusch, speaking second-hand, says "there was all these anti-grav groups up until the early sixties and then they, you know, totally vaporized." He puts the end a little later than the 1950s and does not choose between the two readings.
